Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 (Hopper humming path), 200-req poisson smoke, ORC

Nemotron NVFP4 + general workload + CPU KV offload. Uses SimpleCPUOffloadConnector (the connector the vLLM Nemotron recipe prescribes), NOT the v0.26 OffloadingConnector used by exps 1-3: the latter asserts tokens_per_chunk %% tokens_per_block == 0, which crashes on this hybrid model's forced 2128-token attention block. SimpleCPUOffloadConnector has no block_size constraint. Pool = 10 GiB (cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank), NOT the recipe's 220 GiB, because the vLLM pod is capped at 128 GiB RAM (220 would OOM-kill); 10 GiB still far exceeds the general workload's spillover. lazy_offload=false. Plus chunked prefill. max_model_len=8192 (matches exps 1-3) is REQUIRED for the offload test: with the model's native 1M ctx, vLLM's boot floor forces a >=1M-token cache (util>=0.364) that dwarfs the workload and never overflows; capping at 8192 lowers the floor so a small cache is legal. gpu_mem=0.345: the OffloadingConnector reserves a ~1 GB CUDA staging buffer, so non-KV memory is ~26.9 GiB (measured, offload ON) -> bootable floor is util~0.342, not the 0.325 that offload-OFF math suggested. At 0.345 the GPU cache is ~71k tokens: boots (8x above the 8192 seq floor) yet below the ~161k-token retained multi-turn set of all 45 general clients, so conversations overflow the cache and evict to CPU. Computed for THIS model (not borrowed from Qwen): weights+activation ~25.6 GiB leave a thin KV cushion of ~133k tokens (~4x one prefill batch, above the ~0.327 bootable floor). That is far smaller than the retained multi-turn KV of all 45 general clients (~160k+ tokens by ~5 turns), so accumulating conversations overflow the GPU cache and evict to the CPU pool, driving cpu_cache_usage > 0. Hybrid Mamba's tiny KV/token (~3 KB, only 6/52 layers hold attention KV) means offload can't be forced by shrinking cache alone the way it can for dense Qwen; the multi-turn retention is the eviction driver.
